source.file: 015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Greetings travelers and welcome back to Goldbound. In today's challenge, we can't leave the Dark Moon Fair until we've earned enough gold to purchase a brand new WoW token and the current price 329,000 gold. Now, we do have a few housekeeping things to do before we jump in there because if you're new here, I've been exploring Azeroth on my Rogue Goldilocked one zone at a time with each new zone unlocked only after purchasing a brand new WoW token. But our challenge today is a little different because last episode we accidentally stepped foot into a locked zone and the forfeit of that misstep, well, our dark moon fair banishment. So to make things fair, we have zero listed auctions and zero items in our bags. Everything is stored away in the bank safely for when we come back. And I've even deposited all my gold, silver, and copper into the Warband Bank. So, we're heading in with nothing. That means whatever gold we make here, we're earning it from zero.
source.canonical_file: goldbound/015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.txt
source.original_file: goldbound/original-vtt/015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.vtt

records.guide: This Faire challenge combined fishing, vendor resales and daily ticket quests, starting with no stored gold or items. It eventually earned a token after a full week of play; it was not one isolated farm.

records.name: Lhara pet/mount resale check

source.file: 015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.txt
source.quote: So, first up, there's Lahara, who does sell mounts and companions, which that title right off the bat speaks gold. And these are some of the more iconic ones from the fair. But unfortunately, all of these mounts and all of the pets that Laara sells are soulbound. So, we might pick them up down the road if we want a new mount for Goldie. For now, while we're locked here, we need to focus purely on profit. And these can't be sold, so they're off the list. Now, next is Dron Dawnrest. This is the heirloom vendor. And these for sure could be handy for alts in the future of warbounded leveling. But the value of heirlooms isn't really what it used to be because back in the day heirlooms would increase the experience you gain by a flat percentage whereas now they only increase how fast you gain rest XP and how slowly you lose it. So not really a flat percentage anymore.

records.name: Replica armor vendor market research

source.quote: And since our leveling progress on Goldilock is slow anyways, we pretty much always have a full rested XP bar. So not exactly a big ticket item for us to buy. But then travelers, we come to Barum. And Barum sells replica armor. And this is where things get interesting because these are bind on equip, which means they can be sold. And they all cost between 55 and 75 tickets each. But the market values do vary widely. Anywhere from 40,000 to 100,000 gold for certain pieces that he sells. Now, that's average listed price. But if you look at the sale data, most of these do sell between 7,000 and 40,000 gold, depending on the piece and the timing, of course. But we're here for a week.

source.file: 015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.txt
source.quote: There are a few daily quests we can do around the fair. These in particular are for some of the carnival games, but the only problem is playing the games isn't free. And checking the ticket booth, they're asking for a few gold for a handful of game tokens. Luckily, we just so happened to have a little bit of a loophole. So, during our molten core runs a few weeks back, we actually equipped a trinket that upon looking at it actually sells for six gold. And that is going to be our starting capital here. We can vendor it, which isn't exactly much, but it's enough to get into the games and start earning our first tickets. Now, for players without restrictions on their accounts, they can earn up to 278 tickets per Dark Moon Fair week. That's more than we're going to be able to do because that assumes you've got high level battle pets to battle the master pet tamers. And spoiler alert, our rag tag squad isn't exactly winning any pet battles against level 25 master tamers. And those alone would give you 105 tickets if you did both every day for seven days. Now, there's also dungeon and PvP quest books that send you out into the world to collect items for another 40 tickets each, but that would also require leaving the fair. So, those are off limits for us, which leaves us with the daily fair mini games. And there's six total, and we can do each one every day for one ticket each. First up is Wackanol, which is technically called Hammer Time. And there's a simple objective. Score 25 points by whacking nooles as they pop up with double points awarded if you hit the one that looks like Hoger. So, we've got this one unlock. Next up, Battle Tanks. A simple but surprisingly fun miniame. Kind of reminds me of the old Mario Kart balloon battle mode, and it's pretty easy to clear. Nothing too crazy. Then there's Ring Toss. And this one's tough. You have to wait for the turtle to drift close to the gate, time the cast perfectly, and predict if it's going to speed up or swerve. In my opinion, this is the hardest of the bunch, but I think we still got it unlock. And after that, arguably the most fun, the dance battles. This is basically just a memory game with multiple difficulty levels and probably my favorite of the set. It's just nice to see Goldie out there, you know, having a good time in the dance floor. And then there's the shooting gallery, a classic carnival style game where you just have to hit targets as they appear, fast and simple and easy.
source.canonical_file: goldbound/015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.txt

source.file: 015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.txt
source.quote: One ticket per day. And finally, maybe more dangerously, is the cannon shot, where they literally fire you out of a cannon and you've got to land on the ring on the water below. Once you get the hang of this one though, it's an easy daily turn in. So, as far as the mini games go, our goal is clear. Make sure we hit all six of these every day to secure our tickets. And beyond that, there's also a few one-time profession quests that give you a bunch of tickets. We get one for each of our primary professions and other ones for our secondary professions. So, right now, we're still running tailoring and enchanting from the Westfall shuffle. And of course, we have fishing. So, we'll go ahead and finish up the tailoring enchanting lunge. They're pretty straightforward and just straight up grant a little bit of gold, a little bit of XP, and some tickets. But speaking of fishing, the first quest asks us to catch five fish from the fair's waters, which of course, easy quest, easy tickets. But travelers, that's not where fishing ends at the Dark Moon Fair. Not even close. Because fishing in these waters can also pull up a variety of items. A major one being the Dark Moon Dagger Maw. And this is a special fish that acts like a secondary currency. And not only that, it can be sold on the auction house for about 10 gold each. And there's a vendor nearby who trades the dagger for all sorts of rewards, mounts, pets, toys, and buoys.

source.file: 015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/015 - I Can't Leave Darkmoon Faire Until I Earn A WoW Token.en-orig.txt
source.quote: These are things we can buy and sell on the auction house. But the real consistent high seller for 25 dagger, you can buy dark moon firewater. And this stuff is valuable. Players use it constantly around the clock because it's one of the only consumables that increases your gathering speed. So, it's a must-have for anyone trying to farm herbs and ore efficiently. Not to mention, it also makes your character slightly larger, which I guess people like as well. But each firewater sells for about 200 to 250 gold and it only comes from the fair. This means it could be one of our best repeatable gold farms this week. But is fishing dagger and flipping into fire water the best method? Well, not exactly. There's an even more efficient angle. You see, all around the fair's coastline are shipwrecked debris pools. And these pools almost always give a sealed dark moon crate which has a 97% chance to contain, you guessed it, a dark moon firewater. And if you fish from these pools, you get two to five dark moon digger per cast. Anyways, now each pool only lasts for about one or two casts before it disappears. So the idea here is to run around the coast hopping from pool to pool to get higher rates of dark moon fire water. I'll do a few laps here to see what we can pull.

source.quote: But good morning, travelers. This mailbox is a great start. 33 fire sold for about 7,000 gold and all, 1300 inky black potions sold for another 9,400 gold. We basically just doubled our cash stack on just these inky black potions, which gives us just under 17,000 gold to start day two. And I think you already know what that means. Time to head back to the fair and reinvest about 95% of that into more inky black potions and get back on the water for a big day of fishing and rare hunting. Except if you look at the time, it's 6:00 a.m. It's Tuesday and apparently there's some big maintenance and the servers are going to go down from 7:00 a.m. to 300 p.m. So our farming might be a little bit delayed today. So, let's get this large quantity of inky black potions back on the auction house. And I'll see you when the servers come back online. All right, travelers. Servers are live and spirits are high. Uh, and not too many potion sales yet today, obviously, since the auction house was down. But the plan for today is simple. We need to farm those 500 Dark Moon Deger to finally buy our aquatic mount. Of course, we'll also take off our daily mini games, but we just have that going in the background now. But we need this aquatic mount because I'm getting real tired of seeing other players swim laps around the Dark Moon Fair while I'm just sitting on the shoreline. And right now there's so many people farming these it's hard to get a pool to ourselves. So the mount would give us a big mobility advantage and maybe even a competitive edge on the firewater circuit. But to fish Dark Moon Degerma, we pretty much just fish in any nonpool water. So, we'll be sitting stationary fishing, and we can pick a strategic location, one near a new rare spawn, specifically the dark moon rabbit. Now, this little guy has a pretty crazy spawn timer, apparently. I haven't seen him yet, but the reports range from 6 hours to 32 hours, so we may not see him. And you only really farm this guy for one thing, himself.

source.quote: But with any fishing farm, it always raises the next question. How does it compare to open water fishing? Well, to find out, we just have to do the simplest test in the world. Sit still and fish. We'll pop our plus seven fishing bobbers to increase our fishing skill. And don't waste your dagger maw on the dark moon donuts that are supposed to give plus 10 fishing because those have been bugs since dragon flight. You just can't use them. Now, while we're fishing here, there's a few extra things you can get from open water. For one, you can actually reel in Dark Moon crates, which means fire water is still on the table. You can also catch some bloated fish, which open up for 4 to 10 more dagger and a bit of pocket change. So, those will definitely add some gold per hour. And another fun drop that we would actually love to get is the Dark Moon fishing cap. Now, this one is not only extremely fashionable, but it grants plus five fishing. It also has an onuse ability on a 1-hour cool down that spawns an extra shipwreck debris pool right next to you. So, yeah, we want this one. But the drop rate, it's just 009%. But guess what, travelers? We actually pulled it today.

source.quote: So now we can spawn in shipwreck debris whenever we want. Well, at least every hour. And that extra fishing skill might even increase how often we get sharks and chests. And of course, while we're open water fishing, if you position yourself right, a few random pools should spawn in front of you, which we of course will snag up before anyone else grabs them. But with all that in order, what are the results for 1 hour of openwater fishing? Well, we pulled in 22 Dark Moon Firewaters, which is valued at 5,216 gold. And we also got 310 Daggerma, worth 3,361 gold and about 200 gold in looted currency, which puts our total gold per hour at around 8,776. All while barely moving. So, roughly 58% as efficient as a good day doing pool routes. but it's good to have in your back pocket because if competition is high on the pools, you might actually earn just as much sitting still and fishing the open water. Either way, there's a lot of fishing going on here, travelers. But enough of that. Now, let's talk about tickets. We're of course still doing our dailies every day here at the fair, but there's actually a few other ways we can snag some instant tickets. And with our growing stockpile of Dark Moon Daggerma, we can start the next one. The same vendor who sold us our aquatic mount actually sells a treasure map for 100 Dramma. And now this quest can only be completed once per character, but it's honestly one of the most enjoyable little mystery scavenger hunts in the game. And I hadn't done it before this week and I didn't use a quest helper. I just followed the clues and a little help from my stream chat. Honestly, it was a blast. Now, I don't want to spoil it for you because of how much fun I had. Now, if you do want to see the full playthrough, but don't want to do it yourself, I will be posting the stream segment where we uncover all the mysteries on my second channel, and I'll link that in the description below. But honestly, if you haven't done it yet, I'd really recommend giving it a go yourself. It's a fun one to experience firsthand. But anyways, the reward at the end gives a whopping 100 tickets, which is more than enough to start investing in some transmog gear that we can hopefully sell, I guess, this week. But that's not the only way to get a few extra tickets. There's also a fight arena that has boats every 3 hours, and the rules are pretty simple.

source.quote: And if we snag one of those high value battle pets, well, we could be leaving here today. But travelers, today the pools got extremely competitive, and the more competitive they get, the less efficient they get. So, we need something a little more efficient than just looping the coast on our underwater mount. And guess what? I think I found it. So, every time we pass by the dock, there's a raceway track, and there's a daily quest there that lets you grab one of four race mounts. The one we want, though, is the Mechano Strider. You don't even have to cast anything or pay any ride tickets. If you just walk over it, you get it. And the strider gives you two abilities. One that launches you forward and lets you walk on water for 3 seconds with a speed boost. And another one that launches you high and gives you a parachute to glide down. So now every loop when we pass through the docks, we can grab this mount and blast forward, moving to the next available pools way faster than normal, which is really good bad luck prevention if there's no pool for the whole shore. Now, of course, we can't fish while mounted on it, but it does drastically drop the time between pools, especially in higher volume times. And then every 30 minutes when our Hearthstone comes off cooldown, we can Hearthstone back to Stormwind to post our auctions and run an undercut scam to make sure our dance sticks, inky black potions, and other dark moon goods are always the lowest on the auction house. We have to make sure we're selling all of these if we're going to get out of here. And to be honest, travelers, that's pretty much the loop I ran all day today. And to be fair, most of the night as well. A few restocks on black potions here, a few sellouts there, and a whole lot of music in the background. And as far as the rare spawns today, we did get three or four tags on Moon Fang and two tags on the Dark Moon Rabbit, but no luck on the pet drops. Still, after all that fishing and flipping, it's time to take a load off. And I know just the place, the Elite Torren Chieftain Concert. Let's go.

records.guide: Pick up the race Mechano-strider at the docks and use its movement abilities between debris pools. Dismount to fish, then collect another strider when the coastal loop passes the docks again.
